summary.intent: Resolve callisto's open architecture question (library-first vs moon-first), then get implementation of remaining tracks (idempotent apply, PackageId ecosystem ambiguity) onto a spec-driven SDD+TDD workflow that does not rely on the lossy context window, since the user cannot easily catch Rust mistakes themselves.
summary.outcome: Ran research and fact-check workflows that landed on Option C (narrow library-first, moon as reference integration, delete MoonProjectGraphResolver), chose specificity ordering plus a cross-ecosystem diagnostic for Track E, and created a progressive-disclosure doc structure (.claude/semantic-model, ACTIVE.md, archived plan, fixed design doc contradictions) plus a fresh-session starting prompt. No Track B or E code was implemented yet.

repo: Callisto is a Rust monorepo; verification command is `just ci`, and docs/00-design.md is the design spec with 18 invariants.

Constraints: never commit without explicit instruction, never run `callisto publish` against a real registry, TDD red-before-green, and /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto-findings/ lives outside the repo and must never be committed.

Moon's ProjectDependencyConfig edge carries only id, scope, source and via with no version-requirement string, so moon cannot supply the data the cascade logic needs; moon is useful only for project discovery and cross-checking.
The core crates must have no moon dependency and must build for wasm32-wasip1; the stable public contract is the JSON plan, not the Rust API.

PackageId::matches() lets a bare name match packages in any ecosystem; this is intentional for napi-rs polyglot packages, so Track E adds specificity ordering and a diagnostic rather than changing matches().
[[package-set]] uses glob matching via PackagePattern, is exempt from the cross-ecosystem diagnostic, and [[package]] rules always take priority over it.
PackageMatchedNothing exists in error.rs but is never emitted; VersionPlan and PublishPlan are serializable but never persisted.

code.finding: The manifest write loop unconditionally calls handle.write_version(&bump.to, permit)?; it needs an idempotency guard (at-from write, at-to skip but stage, otherwise UnexpectedManifestVersion). Three RED tests exist but GREEN is unwritten.
Rule lookup uses first-match-wins .find() over cfg.packages; it needs specificity ordering (prefixed beats bare) and a post-loop cross-ecosystem diagnostic in ManifestWalkResolver::build.
Section 9.4 and invariant 6 claimed idempotency is provided only by ecosystem tools; both were rewritten to describe two layers (publish via ecosystem tools, apply via callisto's own version check).

workflow: Fan out research agents with model and effort matched to task difficulty (Haiku for well-documented lookups, Sonnet for source reading, Opus for synthesis), then run a separate verification and red-team pass on load-bearing claims.
Fact-check load-bearing citations independently; the verification confirmed the moon claim but showed the cited commit SHA was just the tip of main, not a meaningful pin.
Use progressive disclosure for agent context: a tiny MEMORY.md pointer, an INDEX.md task-to-file dispatch table, topic files, per-track spec@1 files, then source read on demand.
Use a canon (spec) -> vector (plan) -> lambda (implement/review/exit-gate) agent pipeline with fresh-context adversarial gates so correctness does not depend on one agent's context window.
Write acceptance criteria as falsifiable propositions checkable from outside the implementation.
Sequence semantically coupled fixes; use parallel agents for investigation only.

friction: Context-window loss caused repeated drift and bugs, with circular work that produced poor code output.
The user cannot easily review Rust, so mistakes were found late through tests rather than at spec level.
Second workflow launch had to be stopped and relaunched because null was passed instead of the synthesis doc content.
Doc and plan sprawl and contradictions (design doc claiming idempotency was ecosystem-only) risked confusing later sessions.
Line numbers cited in research drifted slightly from actual source.
open_items: Write canon spec@1 files for Track B and Track E, then run the vector and lambda pipeline.
Implement Part B GREEN: idempotency guard in apply_version_plan plus always staging the changeset path regardless of full.exists().
Implement Track E: specificity ordering and the cross-ecosystem diagnostic in walk.rs, with is_prefixed/is_bare helpers if needed.
Emit PackageMatchedNothing / PackageSetMatchedNothing config validation after the workspace walk.
Persist VersionPlan to disk (Release Please pattern).
Fold the MoonProjectGraphResolver deletion, ProjectLocator trait and the secondary decisions into 00-design.md (§0.1, §15, §7.4/7.5, §6.2) if desired.
Decide the fate of the moved matrix spec (.claude/specs/callisto-matrix.md): commit as PLANNED: SPECIFIED or defer.
Run `just ci` after all implementation work and update the plugins to the new pipeline model.
